title: Procore bid management alternatives: prices and who each fits
description: Procore prices bid management by annual construction volume. Six alternatives for invitations, bid leveling and prequalification, with real prices and who pays.
lead: Procore prices on how much construction you run, not on how many bids you send. That is why contractors who only want bid invitations and comparison look elsewhere.
why: Procore does not publish a rate card. It bills an annual fee based on annual construction volume. Third-party sources estimate $15,000 to $30,000 per year for a contractor running $10 million to $50 million of work, with unlimited users.

Its bid management covers bid creation, leveling, prequalification and bid-to-subcontract conversion, and it sits inside the wider Procore platform. It makes the most sense if you will also use Procore for budgets and contracts.

The alternatives below fall into three groups: dedicated bid tools that charge by users, networks where one side pays, and low-cost project tools with bid comparison built in. None replaces the whole Procore platform, so decide first whether you need the platform or only the bidding.

picks.pickIf: You are a GC and want invitations, prequalification, unlimited online plan-room projects and BidTabs leveling in one license, with a Procore or Autodesk BIM 360 integration.
picks.watchOut: The price is not published and scales with users. Invited subcontractors use it free, but it does not find work for subs.

picks.pickIf: Your subcontractors already respond through it and you want built-in prequalification and risk data.
picks.watchOut: GC pricing is a custom quote. Third-party reports range from $3,600 to $5,000 and up, and some GCs report about $22,000 a year.

picks.pickIf: You want free GC access to a large subcontractor pool and can live with paid add-ons for takeoff and estimation.
picks.watchOut: Subcontractors pay by project radius, so some of your subs may prefer another network.

picks.pickIf: You are a small GC who wants bid management and comparison inside a project tool for $49 to $332 a month.
picks.watchOut: It does not send invitations through a large subcontractor database.

picks.pickIf: You want every feature at one price: $199 a month with one user, then $20 per extra internal user, with free portals for subs.
picks.watchOut: There is no free trial. It offers a 30-day money-back guarantee on monthly plans.

picks.pickIf: You are an owner or a GC on large multi-party programs and want bids tied to budgets.
picks.watchOut: It is quote only and built for large, complex programs.

verdict: For a small GC, Contractor Foreman and JobTread are the only options here with published prices and bid comparison included. Confirm they cover what you need.
If your subcontractors already use a bid network, match it: BuildingConnected if they respond through it, PlanHub if they pay for it.
Keep Procore if you already use it for budgets and contracts and bid management is an add-on to a bill you pay anyway. The cost question changes once you are a customer.
